Monica / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking this. Elysium is finalizing the DPA amendment to include SCCs for our EU and UK traffic. Legal asked me to confirm two things from Redwood before we proceed:

1) Which SCC module you expect to execute for EU -> US transfers (Module 2, Module 4, etc.) and the rationale.
2) A short list of documentary evidence / artifacts we can attach to our procurement file (SOC 2 scope, Data Flow diagrams, DPIA summary, audit log samples).

We have a hard deadline to present recommended language to our board next Wednesday, so if you can provide a proposed module + a short attachments checklist and an ETA that would be hugely helpful.

Best,

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: EU/UK transfer approach + what evidence you can provide

Sam — thanks, quick reply with a proposed route and a delivery plan.

Short answer: Redwood proposes Module 2 (seller to controller) for the UK addendum and Module 4 (processor to processor) as the primary path for EU transfers depending on how Elysium chooses to classify the relationship in the DPA. Rationale: Module 2 gives the broadest coverage for controller-controller scenarios and avoids dual-processor complexity; Module 4 is typically used for pure processor-to-processor relationships and aligns with our Dedicated/Private deployment options where customer retains more control.

What we will provide (ETA in parentheses):
- Evidence index (PDF) listing artifacts and exportability (24 hours) — attachment: evidence-index-elysium.pdf
- SOC 2 scope summary and top-line controls mapping (48 hours)
- Redacted DPIA summary + dataflow diagram (72 hours)
- Sample Audit Log extract and retention policy excerpt (48 hours)
- Signed SCC template (DocuSign) once module choice confirmed (we can have a draft within 2 business days)

I attached a short module comparison spreadsheet (redwood-module-matrix-v1.xlsx) with pros/cons per path and a recommended default for fast execution. If Elysium prefers to default to Module 4 for EU and Module 2 for the UK we can prepare both and mark the Procurement preferred path.

Next steps: confirm which classifier (controller/processor) you want on the DPA cover page and whether you need ours to sign as controller or processor for the EU flows. If you want, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the spreadsheet.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-module-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), evidence-index-elysium.pdf (PDF index)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: EU/UK transfer approach + what evidence you can provide

Sam / Monica — brief legal note to help procurement decide.

1) For the UK: Module 2 + a UK-specific addendum is our recommended approach when there is any level of joint decision-making about personal data. Module 2 is faster for Elysium to accept and reduces the need for additional Processor Contracts.
2) For the EU: if Elysium treats Redwood strictly as a processor for the relevant services, Module 4 is workable; however, Module 4 requires clear records demonstrating the processor-to-processor relationship and additional technical evidence (e.g., subprocessor lists, detailed data flow diagrams).

If Procurement is comfortable with slightly more documentation, we can offer to sign Module 2 in both jurisdictions as a convenience path; that is arguably the least operational friction route for cross-border coverage.

Please note: whichever module is selected, our security pack will include a SOC 2 summary, a CAIQ-lite export, and a redacted DPIA + flowchart. If Elysium requires full SIG completion that will take longer (we estimate 10 business days depending on questions).

Legal is happy to join a call and can provide a one-page rationale memo for your board.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
